advisory.finding: The '--include-archived scopes only which dirs are REPORTED; archived dirs stay cheap' comment and the help/doc claim that per-ticket checks 'cost store ACTIVITY, not history' are inaccurate for checks 1 (_check_json_validity) and 2 (_check_create_events): both always walk every archived dir (include_archived=True for the store-wide tally) AND now add a per-dir _dir_is_archived call that runs a full _is_net_archived log scan, so archived tickets are NOT skipped and incur extra work in these two checks.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Note or align the divergence between _terminal_fold's _foldable_event_count guard and compact_cli's preflock<=threshold gate.
evidence: compact.py:138-143 `preflock = sum(... f.endswith('.json') ...)` then `if preflock <= threshold: ... skipping compaction`
leaf.py:151-152 docstring: 'the guard asks the fold's own selection question via compact._foldable_event_count, at horizon 0'
advisory.finding: `_terminal_fold`'s no-op guard uses `_foldable_event_count(dir, now, 0) == 0`, but `compact_cli`'s own skip gate is `preflock <= threshold` where preflock counts ALL live .json events (not just foldable ones). These are different predicates, so the guard can pass (foldable>0) while the underlying fold is still a no-op, or vice versa; the docstring claims the guard 'asks the fold's own selection question' which is only approximately true.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting a corrupt/unparseable ARCHIVED event (marker present) and assert the dir is still visited as active (marker alone never decides even when the log is unreadable).
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:37-38: `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):` / `continue` — a corrupt event file is skipped, so a corrupt ARCHIVED event yields _is_net_archived == False
tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py:170-171 corrupt event is a COMMENT (`9999999999999999999-COMMENT.json`) added to a ticket archived via rebar.archive (its ARCHIVED event parses fine)
ABSENCE: search of the test file for ARCHIVED shows no test writing an unparseable ARCHIVED event; the commit message asserts 'corrupt-archived-event' edge coverage that does not exist
advisory.finding: The commit claims a 'corrupt-archived-event' edge is covered, but no test injects a corrupt/unparseable ARCHIVED event. _is_net_archived silently skips event files that fail to parse (`except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError): continue`), so a ticket whose ARCHIVED event file is corrupt net-confirms as NOT archived and is treated as active by the default walk. This behavior is untested; the only corrupt-event test corrupts a COMMENT on a ticket whose ARCHIVED event still parses cleanly.
scenarios: A ticket archived under an older/buggy rebar whose ARCHIVED event file is truncated or malformed — the scoping decision would silently treat it as active
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: write the .archived marker plus a corrupt ARCHIVED event file, then assert the ticket id appears in _fsck_repair._ticket_dirs(tracker) (default scoping).
